home.title: NetShield
home.headline: Contain threats before they spread.
home.subheadline: NetShield automatically isolates compromised machines and shuts down suspicious processes across your entire fleet — in seconds, not hours.

benefits.title: Instant network isolation
benefits.body: Cut off a compromised machine from the rest of your network in under two seconds — without touching the machine physically or waiting for a ticket.

benefits.title: Automatic process termination
benefits.body: Suspicious processes are identified and terminated the moment they cross your defined thresholds. No manual intervention required.

benefits.title: Full audit trail
benefits.body: Every isolation event, process kill, and policy change is logged with timestamp, machine ID, and triggering rule — ready for compliance review.

how_steps.title: Deploy the agent
how_steps.body: A single lightweight agent installs on each endpoint in minutes. No kernel modules, no reboot required.

how_steps.title: Define your policies
how_steps.body: Set the network behaviour and process thresholds that trigger containment. Start from a template or write your own rules.

how_steps.title: NetShield acts automatically
how_steps.body: When a rule fires, NetShield isolates the machine and terminates the offending processes — then notifies your team with a full incident report.

home.cta_section_body: Start with a free tier — no credit card required. Upgrade when you need more.

features.meta_description: Network isolation under 500ms, keyword-based process detection, centralised dashboard with multi-agent management and tiered licensing — all the capabilities NetShield brings to your security team.
features.headline: Everything your security team needs to contain threats fast.
features.subheadline: NetShield combines a lightweight cross-platform agent with a centralised management server so your team can detect, isolate, and respond — without leaving the dashboard.

cards.title: Automatic network isolation
cards.body: When a containment rule fires, the agent cuts the machine off from the network in under 500 ms. A single exception is preserved: the connection to the management server, so the agent remains controllable and reversible at any time.

cards.title: Pattern-based process detection
cards.body: The agent scans running processes against a built-in set of name patterns covering known ransomware families and crypto-miners. Detection is straightforward pattern-matching: fast, transparent, and fully auditable — no opaque scoring model.
cards.detail: Detection patterns are defined in the agent. Custom keyword lists are not yet supported.

cards.title: Centralised dashboard
cards.body: All agents report to a single management server. From the dashboard you can view live status, trigger manual isolation, release quarantined machines, and review the full event log.
cards.detail: Authenticated access. Multi-agent fleet management from one interface.

cards.title: Tiered licensing
cards.body: NetShield is available in several tiers scaled to the number of agents you need. Start small and scale up as your fleet grows — no vendor lock-in.
cards.detail: See the Pricing page for current tier details.

features.cta_title: Want to see it in action?

how_it_works.meta_description: From licence activation to real-time containment: a step-by-step look at how NetShield's agent, management server, and dashboard work together to protect your fleet.
how_it_works.headline: From install to containment in four steps.
how_it_works.subheadline: NetShield is built around a lightweight agent that runs on each endpoint and a central management server your team controls. Here is the complete flow.

steps.title: Activate your licence
steps.body: After purchase, you receive a licence key. Entering it on the management server unlocks the number of agents your plan allows and enables the dashboard.

steps.title: Install the agent on each endpoint
steps.body: The agent is a single binary — no kernel module, no reboot. Deploy it on Windows, Linux, or macOS machines. Each agent registers with the management server on first start and appears in the dashboard within seconds.

steps.title: The agent stays connected
steps.body: Each agent maintains a persistent connection to the management server. This real-time channel lets the server push commands — isolation, process termination, policy updates — and receive events back from the endpoint.

steps.title: A rule fires — NetShield acts
steps.body: When a process matches a detection rule, the agent terminates it and, if the policy requires it, isolates the machine from the network (a single exception keeps the management connection open). The event is logged immediately and visible in real time on the dashboard.

arch_items.label: Endpoint agent
arch_items.detail: Lightweight binary on each machine. Monitors processes, enforces isolation rules, reports events.

arch_items.label: Management server
arch_items.detail: Central coordination point. Holds policies, licence state, event log. Communicates with agents in real time.

arch_items.label: Dashboard
arch_items.detail: Web interface for your security team. Live fleet view, manual controls, full audit log.

trust.meta_description: Transparent answers to the most common security questions about NetShield: Windows SmartScreen warning, VirusTotal scan results, dashboard authentication, and encryption.
trust.headline: Honest answers to your security questions.
trust.subheadline: NetShield manipulates network rules and process tables — which means antivirus engines and OS warnings treat it cautiously. Here is exactly what is happening and why.

sections.title: Why does Windows show an "Unknown Publisher" warning?
sections.body: NetShield is currently distributed without a code-signing certificate. This is a deliberate commercial decision while the product is in its early stage — not a sign that the binary is dangerous. Windows SmartScreen displays this warning for any unsigned executable, regardless of its actual purpose.
steps: Click "More info" (Informations complémentaires) on the SmartScreen dialog.
Then click "Run anyway" (Exécuter quand même) to launch the agent.
sections.note: A code-signing certificate is on the roadmap and will be obtained as soon as early sales make it financially viable. No date is committed.

sections.title: VirusTotal scan results
sections.body: The final NetShield agent binary was submitted to VirusTotal. Result: 4 detections out of 71 antivirus engines tested.
sections.vt_detail: All four detections are generic or heuristic identifiers — none names a known malware family:

vt_engines.note: A file-hash-based generic identifier, not a named threat.
A heuristic confidence score, not a malware family name.
"ML" = machine learning signal. A generic behavioural attribute, not a named threat.

sections.vt_negative: Windows Defender, Kaspersky, ESET, BitDefender, Avast, Malwarebytes, Sophos, Trend Micro: all returned negative.
sections.vt_context: This detection profile is typical for any unsigned binary that manipulates network interfaces or process tables — regardless of its actual intent. NetShield does both by design.

sections.title: Dashboard authentication
sections.body: Access to the NetShield management dashboard requires a password. Sessions are managed via a secure cookie. No unauthenticated access to agent controls or event logs is possible.

sections.title: Communications encryption
sections.body: Whether the traffic between agents and the management server is encrypted depends on how you deploy the server. If you place the server behind a reverse proxy with a valid TLS certificate (recommended), all communications will be encrypted over HTTPS. The agent code itself does not enforce TLS — this is a deployment responsibility.
sections.note: We recommend always running the management server behind HTTPS in production.

trust.cta_body: Reach out via the support page.

The NetShield server package you received after purchase.

steps.title: Create your configuration file
steps.body: Copy the example configuration file to create your real one.

steps.title: Install Python dependencies
steps.body: Run pip to install all required packages.

steps.title: Run database migrations
steps.body: Apply all database schema migrations before starting the server for the first time.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.body: Launch the server from the server/ directory.

steps.title: Note your admin password
steps.body: On the very first start, NetShield creates an admin account automatically. If the ADMIN_PASSWORD environment variable is not set, a random password is generated and printed once in the server logs. Copy it immediately — it will not be shown again.

faq.meta_description: Frequently asked questions about NetShield: agent not connecting, lost admin password, multi-machine licences, and more.
faq.headline: Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: Why does my agent not appear in the dashboard after installation?
items.a: The most common cause is a mismatch between secret_key in the agent's config.json and the NETSHIELD_SECRET_KEY variable on the server. Both values must be exactly identical, character for character. Double-check both files and restart the agent after correcting.

items.q: The server refuses to start — what should I do?
items.a: Check the CORS_ORIGINS value in your .env file. It must be a valid JSON array, for example ["https://my-domain.com"]. An invalid format (missing quotes, trailing comma, plain text) will prevent the server from starting.

items.q: I lost the admin password generated at first start. How do I reset it?
items.a: Restart the server with the ADMIN_PASSWORD environment variable explicitly set to your new password. The server will use that value instead of generating a new random one.

items.q: Can I install the agent on multiple machines with the same licence?
items.a: Yes — up to the agent limit of your licence tier. The exact number depends on the plan you purchased. The dashboard shows how many agents are currently active against your limit.

items.q: Windows shows a warning when I launch the agent. Is it dangerous?
items.a: No. This is a Windows SmartScreen warning that appears for any executable without a code-signing certificate. See the Trust & Security page for the exact steps to proceed.

items.q: What happens if my Payhip subscription is cancelled?
items.a: The licence is deactivated on the server. Existing agents lose authorisation to operate at their next validation check. Renewing the subscription reactivates the licence.

troubleshooting.meta_description: Diagnose and fix the most common NetShield issues: invalid licence, server not starting, agent connected but dashboard empty.
troubleshooting.headline: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.subheadline: Step-by-step solutions for the most common issues encountered during installation and operation.

issues.symptom: "Invalid licence" error when the agent starts
issues.cause: The licence key may have been copied incorrectly from the Payhip confirmation email.
issues.solution: Open config.json and verify that license_key exactly matches the key in your email — no leading or trailing spaces, no missing characters. Copy-paste directly from the email rather than retyping.

issues.cause: The server cannot reach the database at the address specified in DATABASE_URL.
issues.solution: Verify that PostgreSQL (or SQLite) is running and accessible at the connection string in your .env file. Check for typos in the host, port, database name, or credentials. For PostgreSQL, confirm the server is accepting connections from the host where NetShield is running.

issues.symptom: The agent connects but the dashboard remains empty
issues.cause: The c2_server URL in config.json may not be pointing at the correct endpoint.
issues.solution: Check that c2_server ends exactly with /api/v1. Example: https://your-server.example.com/api/v1. Missing the path suffix is the most common cause of this symptom.
